basics.summary: B.Tech CSE (AI & ML) student (Batch 2027) with strong foundations in programming, data structures, and problem solving. Hands-on experience in building real-world applications using modern software development practices and AI/ML technologies. Seeking internship or entry-level opportunities to learn, contribute, and grow in a professional engineering environment.

bullets: Developed an AI-Powered Mental Health Companion using Streamlit to create an interactive and accessible web application.
Implemented a multi-modal machine learning system using TensorFlow and DeepFace to analyze facial, voice, and text inputs for emotional state understanding.
Built real-time processing workflows to simulate intelligent behavioral insights and improve user interaction.
Focused on integrating AI models with a functional frontend to understand practical deployment of machine learning systems.

projects.title: AI-Powered Mental Health Companion
projects.stack: Full Stack & AI, Streamlit, TensorFlow, DeepFace
bullets: UI & Accessibility: Developed a highly responsive web application using Streamlit, featuring a high-contrast, intuitive interface designed for accessibility across diverse user groups.
Complex Integration: Built a multi-modal fusion engine using TensorFlow and DeepFace to simultaneously analyze Face, Voice, and Text inputs for real-time emotional state assessment.
Safety & Logic: Engineered robust crisis detection algorithms to identify distress signals with 95% accuracy, automatically suggesting emergency resources to prioritize user safety.

projects.title: Deep Learning Based Animal Detection on Railway Track
projects.stack: Python & Computer Vision, YOLOv8, OpenCV, Tkinter, Pushover API
bullets: Real-Time Detection: Developed an automated monitoring system using YOLOv8 and OpenCV to detect animals on railway tracks, reducing potential accidents.
System Architecture: Designed a user-friendly GUI using Tkinter for video analysis and integrated the Pushover API to send instant alerts to authorities upon detection.
